_: MAHWORLD WORLD 01 — THE FIXED DIAGNOSTIC CAMERA SUITE (WORLD01_MASTER.md sections 13 and 27).
This is data, not a script, because the master file names the camera suite as its own ownership
boundary and because every evidence run in this project has so far carried its own private copy
of the cameras. Two tables describing one view is how evidence stops being comparable between
passes: a 'sightline' rendered last week from a slightly different position is not a before.
One file, read by whatever harness is running.
EVERY POSITION IS DERIVED FROM A REAL WORLD COORDINATE, not eyeballed. The sites are
buildings.js SITES — gym (-58,-10), market (62,-34), match (0,-74) — the ascent pads are
fobeam.js ASCENTS (-30,-22), (32,-18), (-13,-37), the monument is monument.js SITE (0,-6.5),
and MAH NEXUS stands at bearing 126 / radius 1750, world (-1028.6,-1415.8). If a site moves,
the camera aimed at it should move with it and this file should be corrected, not re-guessed.
Render ONLY the views needed to judge the active correction (master section 13).

plaza-hero.why: 1. MAIN PLAZA HERO — the arrival frame: central monument plus the three facilities.

building-away.why: 2. BUILDING-AWAY — stand beside MAH MARKET (62,-34) and look AWAY from its facade, out past the plaza's east flank. This is the master file's core spaciousness test: the eye must find world depth, not another wall.

long-sightline.why: 3. LONG SIGHTLINE — standing ON the deck looking deep into the world. Telephoto on purpose: a wide lens flattens midground and background into the same patch.

monument-close.why: 4. MONUMENT CLOSE — proves Mr. Mah / Mrs. Mah anatomy and material. Raised to the figures' own height rather than shot from the deck, so the read is the sculpture and not the plinth.

monument-34.why: 5. MONUMENT 3/4 — silhouette and premium metal response from three-quarters, where a statue either has a back and a side or does not.

backside.why: 6. BACKSIDE / OPPOSITE DISTRICT — behind MAH MATCH looking back over the plaza. Proves the world is 360 degrees and not a stage set.

high-overview.why: 7. HIGH OVERVIEW — density, spacing and district organisation in one frame: the deck, city.js's 126-620 m ring and terrain.js's land beyond.

dome-vastness.why: 8. DOME VASTNESS — low, with deck-scale reference in the foreground, looking up and out across the enclosed volume. The dome must read as a containing world shell, not a ceiling over the city.

void-bridge.why: 9. VOID / BRIDGE — an elevated route crossing open span with the world below and beyond it.

distant-district.why: 10. DISTANT DISTRICT — MAH NEXUS on bearing 126 at 1750 m, seen from the deck. Enough space between here and there to communicate real travel.

floor-text.why: 11. FLOOR-TEXT LEGIBILITY — shallow angle at walking height over the plaza wordmark, which is the angle that exposes text buried under an overlay or fighting the deck for depth.

match-anchor.why: 13. MATCH ANCHOR — MAH MATCH (0,-74) and its tower from the MAH MARKET approach, on a diagonal because the monument stands dead on the plaza axis. ADDED after a form pass on that tower rendered three suite views with byte-identical triangle counts: the district's tallest silhouette, the thing buildings.js calls 'the anchor from anywhere', was not visible from a single camera in the suite. A landmark with no diagnostic view cannot be judged, so it cannot be corrected.

color-contrast.why: 12. COLOR / CONTRAST HERO — the neutral silver/graphite/black foundation with its purple, sky-blue and clean-red accents, and the frame to check for yellow/orange/amber contamination.
